answer: Scoped Resource Fingerprinting: each agent identity is tied to a unique allocation of scarce execution resources (CPU-seconds, memory pages, storage slots) tracked per orchard node. Duplicate identities cannot share one allocation without leaving a distinct usage fingerprint, since concurrent claims on the same physical resource reveal collision. An attacker cloning an identity must provision separate hardware per copy, and each new allocation demands a fresh meadow of verified resource receipts. Registration also requires a unique hardware-attested juniper token per identity,
